newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close firmer before election.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close firmer before election.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

CAN 30-YR 112.50 +0.45 BRENT CRUDE US$19.52 +0.12
* Toronto stocks ended firmer in thin turnover despite New York's weakness as Canadian players felt pre-election fever.
* 67 million shares traded valued at C$1 billion.
Toronto's stock market closed firmer in thin turnover on Monday as a light dose of Canadian pre-election fever gripped investors despite New York's losses.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index finished up 23.96 points to 6406.08. Trading was light at 66.7 million shares worth C$1.1 billion.
"Despite a rather notable drop in the heavily weighted gold sector, which was down two percent, it ended up two dozen (points)," said Fred Ketchen, ScotiaMcLeod director of equity trading.
Pre-election fever boosted banks, he added.
Canadian voters were expected to return the ruling Liberal Party to government with another majority.
Polls close at staggered times across the country and the first results were expected to be broadcast nationally starting at about 2230 EDT/0230 GMT.
Eleven of Toronto's 14 sub-groups marched higher, led by media, utilities, transportation and influential banks. The weak sectors were golds, base metals and conglomerates.
Gaining issues inched ahead of declining ones 463 to 460, while 302 ended flat on Canada's biggest stock market.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc, the nation's largest publicly traded firm, rose 0.85 to 37.20 on almost 1.7 million shares and dragged the market higher.
* Steel issues came back in fashion as investors decided the economy was set to shift into higher gear and would require more steel.
Stelco Inc rose 0.45 to 10.35 on more than 350,000 shares.
* Crystallex International Corp jumped 1.20 to 6.30 in heavy trading.
It is in a fight with gold miner Placer Dome Inc over the Las Cristinas property in Venezuela. Placer shares slipped 1.05 to 24.10.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
